newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha higher, contango broadens.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha higher, contango broadens.

text.p: Naphtha prices firmed in afternoon Tokyo trade in tandem with overnight European markets, while the contango in inter-month spreads steepened amid a persistent supply surplus in prompt cargoes, traders said on Thursday.
Second-half July open-specification naphtha was sold by a European trader at $211.25 per tonne in early afternoon trade.
On Wednesday the contract traded at $209.50.
First-half July was assessed 75 cents to $1.00 lower than second-half July.
Earlier this week, first-half July was quoted almost on par with the second-half of the month.
Sentiment in the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market strengthened with Indonesian inventories declining steadily.
Indonesian stockpiles, which ballooned after a fire closed a hydrocracker at the Dumai refinery in April, have been shrinking due to brisk May demand, fuel oil traders said.

Pertamina's regional customers, such as Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and India, have bought a combined three million barrels of May-lifting cargoes, the traders said. About one million barrels are believed to have been destined for the United States, 600,000 barrels for Italy, and 500,000 barrels for Australia, they said. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
